title: Playing with Punch and Jack Carey; Crowback and others
summary: Vincent describes the break-up when Punch Miller took over Jack Carey's band, and the sidemen around it, including saxophonist Crowback and Peter Bocage.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did you play with Jack any?

Huh? You played with Jack some time, huh? Jack? Oh yeah. Yeah, I remember his band when you remember. But you quit him and you taken all that from him, you see? And we went with you. And you know how the two down there was Linton come saying that's bad, well that's how it broke us up, you see? And then we got together and we worked with different other fellas. That's what broke his bad enough, you know? Yeah, I had a job in the country for Austin and Johnny Henry. And then it was Crowback. And he couldn't come to eat. You remember Crowback, don't you? Yeah. He was a clownist player in the psych. And then you remember Kit Harris? Remember him, eh? Johnny Harris, you know? Who was Crowback? And then Cato Harry, big, big, big, big, big. Yeah, I know him. Yeah. And then there was Peter Boquet.

He said who was Crowback? Crowback was a saxophone player. For about seven years, he looked something like a white boy, you know? What was his last name? What was his last name? Crowback? That's his last name, Crowback. I forget his first name. I forget his first name. How many things? Huh? Yeah. He said he forget his first name. Who did he play with? He had much to carry with us a lot. Who did he play with? Crowback. Crowback. He was playing with us. We had, you know, this is making up a band. Sometimes we were high, and when I was with Tom I was, kid I was in the Bronx band. We were high, you know. We were high, you know. And, and I played with Peter Boquet with a band too, you know. But he didn't last long. Then Mud Carter, he come with us for a while. Then he left, went back, and he come back and played with Jack. That's where he come in after he left then. And then Mud Carter, he had a band of himself. And this fella I can't think of. King or someone? Well I just said that to make me remember. King, tell him King.
